matter_reference_date_basis: Taken from the matter file: exam session OCTOBER 2024, matter_reference_date 2024-10. The law is stated as at that session.
corpus_gaps: No regulation, Order or rate schedule prescribing the rate of stamp duty on an instrument of transfer of immovable property in the Western Province is in the corpus; s.37 of the Financial Statute of the Western Province, No. 6 of 1990 charges duty only at the prescribed rate and s.77(1)(a) leaves the rate to regulations published in the Gazette. Without it the money amount of the duty cannot be calculated.

The Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982 is in the corpus without any rate schedule, and the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No. 12 of 2006 likewise fixes rates only by Ministerial Order under s.3, which is not in the corpus.

The commencement dates of the Financial Statute of the Western Province, No. 6 of 1990 (which s.1 leaves to Ministerial Order for each Part) and of the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024 are not recorded in the corpus, so their operation at 2024-10 is inferred from the corpus in_force_from_year and amendment_events rather than from a commencement Order.

No provincial statute for any Province other than the Western Province is in the corpus, so the conclusion that Kalutara District falls within the Western Province rests on general geography rather than on a provision reached through the search tool; the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution is not in the corpus.

The corpus text of the Financial Statute of the Western Province is visibly imperfect optical character recognition (for example s.37 reads 'a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province'); excerpts are verbatim as to the corpus but the underlying print should be checked against the Gazette text.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: Stamp duty on a deed of gift of land is a creature of statute and subsidiary legislation: the charging section, the definition of the chargeable value, the person liable and the payment and attestation procedure are all found in the Financial Statute of the Western Province, No. 6 of 1990, the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No. 12 of 2006 and the Notaries Ordinance. No judicial authority or Roman-Dutch doctrine is needed. The one gap is subsidiary legislation rather than case law: the Gazette regulation prescribing the rate is not in the corpus.

legal_issues.issue: Which enactment charges stamp duty on a deed of gift of land situated at Kalutara, and at what rate.
What is the "value" on which the duty is computed where the donor acquired the land in 1995 and built the house himself, and how does that value relate to the present market value.
Who is liable to pay the duty, and what is the procedure for payment, stamping, attestation and the consequences of under-stamping.

questions.hop_count_basis: Charging section (s.37) to the definition of "transfer" that brings a gift within it (s.106), to the valuation rule (s.48(1)) and from there to the definition of "value" for gifted immovable property acquired after 31 March 1977 (s.106 paragraph (c)), and finally to the prescribed rate (s.77) and the payment and attestation provisions (s.40, s.51, Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (7A)). Four necessary linked steps across two enactments.

enrichment.original_background: In 1995 Shantha Silva purchased a land in extent of 10 perches situated in Kalutara for Rs.700,000/- and constructed a house on it. The cost of construction of the house was Rs.2,000,000/-. He wishes to gift this house and land to his daughter Sumana and he instructs you to prepare a Deed of Gift in this regard. The present market value of the house and property is Rs.10,400,000/-.

gold_answer_draft.issue: What stamp duty is chargeable on a deed of gift by which a father gifts to his daughter a 10-perch land at Kalutara that he bought in 1995 for Rs.700,000 and on which he built a house at a cost of Rs.2,000,000, the present market value being Rs.10,400,000; on what value is the duty computed, who pays it, and what is the procedure for payment and attestation.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Kalutara is in the Western Province, so stamp duty on an instrument relating to a transfer of this land is charged by the Financial Statute of the Western Province, No. 6 of 1990. Section 37 charges duty at the prescribed rate on every instrument relating to a transfer of immovable property situated in the Province, and s.106 defines "transfer" to include a gift and "gift" as a voluntary transfer without consideration in money or money's worth. Section 48(1) requires the duty to be calculated on the value of the property conveyed. For immovable property that is gifted and that the donor acquired after 31 March 1977, s.106 defines "value" as the lower of (i) the price the property would have fetched in the open market on the date the donor acquired it, increased by the cost of improvements, alterations and additions made after acquisition and before the gift, and (ii) the price it would fetch in the open market at the date of the instrument of gift. The rate applied to that value is a prescribed rate, that is a rate fixed by regulation of the provincial Minister published in the Gazette under s.77(1)(a). By s.51(a) the duty on an instrument of transfer is payable by the grantee. Section 40(1) requires payment before or at the time of execution; s.40(2) allows payment for a transfer of immovable property to a prescribed bank, which issues a certificate of payment that is affixed to the instrument, and permits payment within seven days of execution where earlier payment was impossible for reasons beyond the payer's control. Section 9 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No. 12 of 2006 directs the duty to the Provincial Council within whose limits the property is situated, and to a bank prescribed by the Commissioner-General while the Council stands dissolved. Section 78(1) requires the deed to set out the parties, the consideration and all facts affecting chargeability together with the amount of duty, and s.78(2) requires the attesting notary to satisfy himself that the value stamped represents the value of the property. Under the Notaries Ordinance, s.31 rule (6) the notary may not attest a deed unless he has an assurance that the required duty is provided, and rule (7A) requires the notary to pay the duty, to affix the original bank receipt to the duplicate and copies of it to the original and the protocol. Section 39 of the Statute exempts certain instruments, none of which covers a gift between private persons, and by s.60 an instrument that is not duly stamped cannot be registered, authenticated or acted upon except on payment of the deficit and a penalty. Section 62 allows the proper duty to be adjudicated in advance by an Assessor on payment of a fee of two hundred and fifty rupees.
gold_answer_draft.application: The donor acquired the land in 1995, which is after 31 March 1977, so paragraph (c) of the definition of "value" governs. The first measure is the open-market price at acquisition, for which the Rs.700,000 paid in 1995 is the figure on the facts, increased by the Rs.2,000,000 spent on constructing the house, which is an addition made after acquisition and before the gift: Rs.700,000 + Rs.2,000,000 = Rs.2,700,000. The second measure is the open-market price at the date of the deed, Rs.10,400,000. The Statute takes the lower, so the deed is chargeable on Rs.2,700,000 and not on Rs.10,400,000. The duty is then the prescribed rate applied to Rs.2,700,000. Two qualifications should be noted. The Rs.700,000 is the price actually paid in 1995, whereas the Statute speaks of the price the property would have fetched in the open market at that date in the opinion of the Assessor, so the Assessor may substitute a different figure. And the rate to be applied is fixed by a Gazette regulation which is not part of this corpus, so the money figure cannot be stated from the materials available here. The deed falls within no exemption in s.39.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The deed of gift is chargeable with Western Province stamp duty on a value of Rs.2,700,000, being the Rs.700,000 acquisition price plus the Rs.2,000,000 cost of construction, that being lower than the Rs.10,400,000 present market value. The duty payable is the prescribed rate applied to Rs.2,700,000; the rate regulation is outside this corpus, so the figure is left open rather than stated. The duty falls on the donee unless the deed provides otherwise. In practice the notary computes the duty, pays it to the prescribed bank before or at the time of execution, affixes the original receipt to the duplicate and copies to the original and the protocol, sets out in the deed the facts affecting chargeability and the amount of duty, and attests only once satisfied that the duty has been provided and that the value stamped is the value of the property. If the deed is insufficiently stamped it cannot be registered or acted upon until the deficit and a penalty are paid; where the value is doubtful the proper duty can be adjudicated in advance by an Assessor.

answer_claims.claim_text: A deed of gift of land situated in the Western Province is an instrument relating to a transfer of immovable property situated in that Province and is chargeable with stamp duty under the Financial Statute of the Western Province, No. 6 of 1990, s.37, because s.106 defines "transfer" to include a gift.
The duty is calculated on the value of the property conveyed (Statute s.48(1)).

Where immovable property acquired by the donor after 31 March 1977 is gifted, "value" in s.106 means the lower of (i) the open-market price at the date the donor acquired it increased by the cost of improvements, alterations and additions made before the gift, and (ii) the open-market price at the date of the instrument of gift.
The rate itself is a prescribed rate, fixed by regulation made by the provincial Minister and published in the Gazette (Statute ss.37 and 77(1)(a)).
The duty on an instrument of transfer is payable by the grantee, that is the donee (Statute s.51(a)).

Payment must be made before or at the time of execution, and for a transfer of immovable property may be made to a prescribed bank which issues a certificate of payment to be affixed to the instrument; where payment beforehand was impossible for reasons beyond the payer's control it must be made within seven days of execution (Statute s.40(1) and (2)).

The notary must pay the stamp duty, affix the original bank receipt to the duplicate and copies to the original and the protocol, may not attest the deed without an assurance that the duty is provided, must set out in the deed the facts affecting chargeability and the amount of duty, and must satisfy himself that the value stamped represents the value of the property (Notaries Ordinance s.31 rules (6) and (7A); Statute s.78(1) and (2)).
Shantha Silva acquired the land in 1995, that is after 31 March 1977, so paragraph (c) of the definition of "value" applies rather than paragraph (b).

The first measure is the open-market price at acquisition, for which the Rs.700,000 paid in 1995 is the evidence available, increased by the Rs.2,000,000 cost of constructing the house, an addition made after acquisition and before the gift, giving Rs.2,700,000.
The second measure is the present market value of Rs.10,400,000 at the date of the deed of gift.
Because Rs.2,700,000 is the lower of the two, the deed of gift is chargeable on a value of Rs.2,700,000 and not on the Rs.10,400,000 market value.
No exemption in s.39 of the Statute covers a gift between private persons, so the deed is not exempt.
The chargeable value of the deed of gift is Rs.2,700,000, being Rs.700,000 plus Rs.2,000,000, that value being lower than the Rs.10,400,000 open-market value at the date of the gift.

The duty payable is the prescribed rate applied to Rs.2,700,000; the regulation fixing that rate for instruments of transfer in the Western Province is not in this corpus, so the money figure cannot be stated from the corpus and the arithmetic is left open.

Procedurally the notary pays the duty to a prescribed bank before or at the time of execution, affixes the original receipt to the duplicate and copies to the original and the protocol, states the facts affecting chargeability and the amount of duty in the deed, and attests only once satisfied that the duty is provided; the duty falls on the donee unless the deed provides otherwise, and an insufficiently stamped deed cannot be registered or acted upon.

questions.block_reason: The question requires the stamp duty to be calculated. The charging provision, s.37 of the Financial Statute of the Western Province, No. 6 of 1990, charges duty at the prescribed rate, and s.77(1)(a) leaves the rate to a regulation published in the Gazette. No rate regulation or rate schedule for instruments of transfer is present in the frozen corpus, and no rate table appears in the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982 or the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No. 12 of 2006 as extracted. The chargeable value of Rs.2,700,000 and the whole method of computation are supported by corpus provisions, but the final money figure cannot be produced without quoting a rate from outside the corpus, which the researcher must not do.
